newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Rebels stall release of captive Colombian troops.
newsitem.headline: Rebels stall release of captive Colombian troops.

text.p: Leftist guerrillas holding at least 60 soldiers prisoner in the jungles of southern Colombia on Thursday dashed hopes of an imminent handover by rejecting government proposals for the release.

Interior Minister Horacio Serpa offered Wednesday to demilitarize a municipality in the southern province of Caqueta for four days to permit the release of the soldiers, who were captured Aug. 30 when guerrillas overran a military base in neighboring Putumayo province.

But a Mexico City-based spokesman for the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) guerrilla force, Marco Leon Calarca, said the government proposal was unacceptable and insisted that two areas should be cleared of troops for at least two weeks.
He said it would be impossible to hand over the captives safely to international mediators in the relatively small area proposed by Serpa.

The government, which accuses the FARC of links to illicit drug operations, believes the prolonged demilitarization of a wide area would give traffickers linked to the FARC the chance to ship in materials used for cocaine production and transport out the finished product.

The FARC, Colombia's largest and oldest guerrilla force, has accused the army of planning to rescue the soldiers by force to avoid the humiliating spectacle of seeing the captives freed under the gaze of the media. Military sources say about 5,000 troops have been drafted into Caqueta, almost double the normal military presence.
